title: Willow & Birch — Security gating & hosting options
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 report, ISO certificate summary, and architecture diagram (Maya) - by 2026-04-03
Customer to circulate security questionnaire answers and data residency constraints (Evan) - by 2026-04-06
Schedule SE-led architecture deep dive and network diagram review - week of 2026-04-06
Set up 2-week pilot with Dedicated instance if gating passes - target start 2026-04-13
action_items: Maya Chen - send SOC2 + ISO summary, pen test overview, and public sec whitepaper - due 2026-04-03
Luis Ortega - prepare deployment diagram showing VPC peering + Private control plane options - due 2026-04-06
Evan Martin - confirm whether BYOK (customer KMS) is required or Redwood KMS acceptable - due 2026-04-06
Jonas Li - provide required audit log retention period and SIEM integration details - due 2026-04-05
summary: Initial security gating call to map Willow & Birch compliance needs to Redwood hosting options. Focus on SOC2/ISO scope, SSO & provisioning, RBAC, audit logs retention, and encryption/KMS choices. Redwood AE + SE to provide docs and an architecture deep dive next week. Customer leaning toward Dedicated but evaluating Private for strict BYOK and data residency.
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on — Maya from Redwood here. Luis from our infra team is with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Evan Martin: Good, thanks. Morning from my side. Evan here, CTO at Willow & Birch. we've got Priya, Jonas and Aisha on as well.
[00:15] Priya Rao: Morning. We'll try to keep this focused — we have a security gating list from legal and infra so want to walk that through.
[00:22] Luis Ortega: Great, we primed a checklist around SOC2, SAML/SCIM, RBAC, audit logs and KMS patterns. happy to dig in and show options across Hosted, Dedicated, Private.

[00:30] Jonas Li: Quick note, our primary constraint is we cannot allow customer PII to be written to third-party persistent stores outside EU for certain flows — data residency matters for some workloads.
[00:38] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll call that out in the options. just to align — are you evaluating for a customer-facing chat assistant and some internal reranking/embeddings workflows?
[00:47] Evan Martin: Yeah, two main use cases: 1) customer chat (PCI-lite, some PII possible), 2) product search and personalization using embeddings. The chat is the gating one.
[00:56] Aisha Qureshi: From procurement side, timeline is roughly end of month for vendor selection — but that depends on how fast security clears things.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Okay noted. I'll share SOC2 and ISO docs straight away. Luis, do you want to run through KMS and BYOK?

[01:12] Luis Ortega: Sure. So we support three encryption patterns: Redwood-managed KMS, Redwood-managed with customer KMS wrap (BYOK wrap), and customer-managed KMS in Private deployments. For Hosted customers we usually do Redwood KMS with dedicated keys per customer — can be region-restricted. In Dedicated we can offer more control and in Private on-prem we fully support customer HSM/KMS integrations.
[01:30] Jonas Li: When you say dedicated keys per customer, does that mean you have separate CMKs in your cloud tenant or you're doing key wrapping with customer keys?

[01:36] Luis Ortega: Good question — for Hosted it's separate CMKs we manage in the cloud region, or we can do a wrap with a customer key if the customer gives a wrapping key. But full BYOK where the key never leaves customer's control is only possible in Private deployments or when we set up a dedicated KMS integration in your account via a partner flow.
[01:54] Priya Rao: So for us, ideally BYOK or an HSM-backed key in our cloud account. we have policies that require us to hold the master key. Is that possible with Dedicated?

[02:03] Luis Ortega: With Dedicated we can provision in a way where keys are either customer-provisioned in the customer's cloud project and we use IAM to access them, or we place the inference nodes in your VPC and then rely on your KMS. There are network steps and audit hooks needed. We'll diagram it.
[02:18] Evan Martin: What about SOC2 scope — does Redwood have SOC2 Type II? and is ISO27001 in scope?

[02:24] Maya Chen: We have SOC2 Type II reports — I'll attach the latest and an ISO27001 summary. note that for Private deployments some controls shift to the customer; we'll identify shared responsibility in the doc.
[02:34] Aisha Qureshi: Procurement will want the statement of applicability and what remains customer responsibility — can you format that for legal?
[02:39] Maya Chen: Absolutely — I'll provide a responsibilities matrix. Luis will add the architecture bits.

[02:45] [03:02] Jonas Li: Another area — audit logs. We need immutable audit logs for admin actions, token usage tracing, and model inference events to ship to our SIEM. retention should be 7 years for admin logs and 2 years for inference traces. How granular are your logs?

[03:18] Luis Ortega: Our runtime emits request/response hashes, request metadata, timestamped lifecycle events (dispatch, batch, model selection) and admin-level events. For Hosted we retain default 90 days in the console but can export to S3/ELK. For Dedicated/Private we can configure retention and forward logs to your SIEM via secure forwarder. We do have an audit log tamper-evidence design and can provide hashes — need to validate exact retention requirements with the engineering team.

[03:45] Priya Rao: Important: we cannot keep full user content in logs beyond 30 days. We need a way to redact PII from inference traces while keeping metadata for performance and billing — is there a redaction or tokenization pipeline?

[03:56] Luis Ortega: There is an optional middleware redaction step before logs are persisted — we can drop or hash content fields and keep non-content metadata. For the pilot we can enable that. note redaction may impact some debugging signals.
[04:10] Evan Martin: Ok. SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. Can we integrate with your RBAC so we can map Okta groups to roles?
[04:17] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Roles can be mapped to SCIM groups and you can configure fine-grained permissions. Luis, anything to add on RBAC?

[04:25] Luis Ortega: Our RBAC model has five built-in roles and supports custom roles with JSON policies. We can restrict API keys by route and model, and enforce token-level audit logs. For Dedicated/Private we can enforce network-level RBAC via VPC controls as well.
[04:40] Jonas Li: Do you support session-level MFA enforcement for console logins? we want enforceable 2FA for admin accounts.
[04:45] Maya Chen: Yes, SSO connects to your IdP so you can enforce MFA and also require device posture if your IdP supports it. We also support granular admin approvals for critical actions.
[04:55] Aisha Qureshi: A couple procurement asks: standard liability limits, data processing addendum, and subprocessor list. Also need to know about any EU data centers for hosting.
[05:05] Maya Chen: We'll provide a DPA template and our subprocessor list. We have EU regions and can pin tenant hosting to EU regions for data residency.

[05:12] Evan Martin: Regarding model fallback and graceful degradation — we need to ensure customer experience if a primary model is unavailable. Are there automatic fallbacks and how are they logged?

[05:20] Luis Ortega: There are routing policies and fallbacks. We log model selection events and fallback occurrences. For Dedicated we can pre-provision fallbacks to meet SLOs without cross-tenant routing.
[05:30] Priya Rao: On the network side: for Private we'd need an on-prem control plane or a VPC peering model. Which one is more common for customers that require strict separation?

[05:38] Luis Ortega: We see two patterns: VPC peering with Private control plane (control plane in Redwood but data plane in your VPC) or fully air-gapped on-prem deployment. Most customers choose VPC peering + Private control plane for the balance of operational overhead and separation.
[05:52] Jonas Li: For the peering option, can we run the inference nodes in our AWS account under our IAM? we want minimal cross-account access.

[05:59] Luis Ortega: That's supported via a dedicated Dedicated placement or private deployment where nodes run in your account — we'll provide the exact IAM roles required. we typically provide a CloudFormation/Terraform template.
[06:10] Evan Martin: Do you run model training or fine-tuning in any of these flows? we only plan to use pre-trained open models, but curious about artifact storage.

[06:18] Maya Chen: Redwood is inference-first; model weights are provided by the model catalog and we do not do customer fine-tuning in Hosted by default. If you need private fine-tuning we can discuss an isolated pipeline with clear data boundaries.
[06:27] Aisha Qureshi: On procurement timing — if everything aligns, we'd expect legal review to take two weeks. If you can provide the requested security packet quickly, that speeds things up.
[06:34] Maya Chen: Will do — SOC2 report, ISO summary, pen test overview, subprocessor list, DPA, responsibilities matrix. Luis will add the hosting diagrams and KMS options.

[06:40] [06:50] Evan Martin: There's one more thing — can you run a short load/latency benchmark to validate latency for 512-token chat interactions? we'll want numbers for p95 under steady state and under burst conditions.

[06:58] Luis Ortega: Yes — we can run a 24-hour benchmark and provide p50/p95/p99 metrics and cost estimates. for the POC we'll instrument KV cache performance, batching effects and cost per 1k tokens. We'll need a sample prompt distribution.
[07:12] Jonas Li: Sample prompts — we'll share a scrubbed set from staging. remember to exclude PII as per our policy.
[07:18] Maya Chen: Great. I'll follow up with an email and attach the docs. any deal-breakers we haven't covered?
[07:24] Priya Rao: BYOK is in the top two. Also immutable audit trail and long retention for admin logs. If we can't get those in Dedicated or Private, it's a blocker.

[07:33] Maya Chen: Understood. We can prioritize BYOK and immutable admin logs in the Dedicated path and show the Private on-prem path as fallback. we'll flag tradeoffs in the responsibilities matrix.
[07:40] Evan Martin: One small question — do you expose token-level cost breakdowns per route for billing reconciliation?
[07:45] Luis Ortega: Yes, Console exposes token-level usage per API key and per route; we can provide breakdown CSVs and integrate with your billing system.
[07:52] Aisha Qureshi: For the pilot price, will you provide a short-term commitment pricing for Dedicated? procurement wants a ballpark to discuss internally.
[07:58] Maya Chen: We'll include a pilot price range in the follow-up and an example dedicated SKU. I'll coordinate with commercial and send a simple term sheet for review.
[08:07] [08:20] Evan Martin: Awesome. Are there any compliance caveats for EU residency we should be aware of?

[08:26] Luis Ortega: The main one is cross-border transfers for debug traces; we can configure regional-only storage and ensure data doesn't leave EU regions for certain tenants. We'll call out any residual telemetry flows.
[08:36] Priya Rao: Last technical ask — can you support automatic PII redaction in the middleware with configurable rules?
[08:43] Luis Ortega: Yes, configurable redaction rules are possible. for the pilot we'll propose a set of common rules and can tune them with Jonas during the POC.

[08:52] Maya Chen: OK wrapping up — recap and owners: I'll send security packet (SOC2, ISO, DPA, subprocessor list) and responsibilities matrix. Luis will produce deployment diagrams and KMS options and run the benchmark. Evan/Jonas will share scrubbed prompt set and retention requirements. procurement (Aisha) will wait for the term sheet.
[09:12] Evan Martin: Sounds good. Thanks everyone. Any final questions?
[09:16] Aisha Qureshi: No, that's it from procurement. we'll look for the DPA and term sheet.
[09:20] Jonas Li: I'll pull together the retention and SIEM integration details and share them by Monday.
[09:26] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with attachments and a proposed time for the architecture deep dive. Bye.
